title: Structured-light-mediated hybrid entanglement between photon polarization and electronic orbital angular momentum
abstract: We propose a minimal quantum-optical scheme for generating hybrid entanglement between photon polarization and electronic orbital angular momentum in a semiconductor quantum disk. A spin--orbit structured two-photon state excites two channels in the same disk: a radiatively recombining zero-orbital-angular-momentum channel and a finite-orbital-angular-momentum channel that stores the electronic orbital qubit. An effective coherent mapping prepares a selected two-excitation state, followed by emission of a photon whose polarization is entangled with the residual electronic orbital state. A master-equation analysis shows that the heralded state conditioned on single-photon occupation of the selected output mode approaches the target entangled state in the ideal coherent limit. We also discuss orbital relaxation and perturbative validity conditions for branch-dependent Coulomb shifts, orbital-angular-momentum mixing, and finite-orbital-angular-momentum radiative leakage. This proof-of-principle effective model suggests a route toward structured-light-mediated photon--electron hybrid entanglement in semiconductor nanostructures.
summary: The paper proposes an effective model demonstrating how structured light can mediate the creation of hybrid entanglement between emitted photon polarization and the orbital angular momentum stored in an electron within a semiconductor quantum disk. By analyzing the system dynamics via master equations, it shows that high fidelity is achievable provided electronic orbital relaxation is slow compared to the emission timescale.
main_problem: The primary goal is generating hybrid entanglement between photon polarization and electronic orbital angular momentum (OAM) using structured light in a semiconductor quantum disk.
main_result: The proposed effective model demonstrates that high-fidelity entanglement can be achieved when the orbital relaxation time significantly exceeds the characteristic emission and detection timescales.
method: The analysis employs an open-system master equation approach to track the system's evolution, calculating heralded entanglement fidelity conditioned on single-photon detection.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a semiconductor quantum disk utilizing two excitation channels: one for radiative recombination (zero OAM) and another storing the electronic orbital qubit (finite OAM). The dynamics are modeled using an effective Hamiltonian and Lindblad dissipators.

FIG. 2. Conceptual illustration of photon–electron hybrid- entanglement generation within a single semiconductor quan- tum disk. The labels A and B denote two optically addressed excitation channels in the same disk: a zero-OAM channel that recombines radiatively and a ﬁnite-OAM channel that stores the residual electronic OAM qubit. A spin–orbit struc- tured two-photon state is mapped to a two-excitation state through optical spin and OAM selection rules. Subsequent radiative recombination of the zero-OAM excitation emits a photon whose polarization is entangled with the residual elec- tronic OAM state.
